candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated attacker fully controls the `from` query parameter of /securityRealm/commenceLogin (and, as fallback, the Referer header) of a link sent to a victim. The value is only checked by getValidRedirectUrl before being stored in the victim's session and used as the post-login redirect target.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The value passes Java URL resolution; absolute URLs are returned unchanged, so the check reduces to a prefix test. With a rootUrl ending in '/' (Jenkins URL configured conventionally), the classic bypasses (`//evil.example`, `https://evil.example/`, `rootUrl.evil.example/`, `rootUrl@evil.example/`) all fail the prefix test, which limits exploitability to deployments whose effective root URL lacks the trailing slash. The logout-page special case (lines 939-942) does not mitigate off-site targets. I could not verify Jenkins core's normalization of the configured root URL nor getRootUrlFromRequest()'s trailing-slash behavior from this snapshot (Jenkins core sources are out of scope), and this prefix-check pattern has long existed in the plugin, so it may be pre-existing/accepted behavior rather than the intended case defect.
candidates.impact: Open redirect after successful authentication: an attacker can direct a freshly authenticated Jenkins user to an attacker-controlled origin that mimics Jenkins. This enables phishing/credential relay and can leak sensitive material carried in the post-login navigation (URL fragments, copied link parameters, or credentials re-entered on a look-alike page); it also undermines the plugin's stated guarantee that 'the login must not redirect outside Jenkins realm' (comment at lines 924-930). No authentication is required to create the malicious link, and the redirect occurs on the trusted Jenkins origin.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) OicSecurityRealm is the active security realm (standard deployment of this plugin). 2) The effective root URL used by getRootUrl() has no trailing '/' — e.g. the documented `rootURLFromRequest=true` option, where the root URL is derived from the request (scheme://host[:port][contextPath]) without a trailing slash, or an administrator-configured Jenkins URL stored without one. 3) Victim completes (or already has) an OIDC login so doFinishLogin runs. In the suffix variant the attacker host is `ci.example.com.evil.example`; in the userinfo variant it is `https://ci.example.com@evil.example/`.
candidates.root_cause: getValidRedirectUrl() builds `new URL(new URL(rootUrl), url)` and accepts any result whose string starts with rootUrl (`redirectUrl.startsWith(rootUrl)`). For an absolute attacker-supplied URL this check is a pure string-prefix test, so any attacker host whose name continues the rootUrl string (userinfo form `rootUrl` + `@evil.example`, or suffix form `rootUrl` + `.evil.example`) passes when rootUrl does not end with '/'. The validated value is persisted in the HTTP session (SESSION_POST_LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL_KEY) by doCommenceLogin and consumed unchanged by doFinishLogin's `response.sendRedirect(...)`.
candidates.title: Post-login open redirect via unvalidated `from`/Referer in OicSecurityRealm.getValidRedirectUrl
candidates.trace: doCommenceLogin(@QueryParameter String from, @Header("Referer") referer) -> getValidRedirectUrl(from != null ? from : referer) (line 964) -> new URL(new URL(rootUrl), url).toString() (line 935) -> `redirectUrl.startsWith(rootUrl)` (line 937) returns attacker URL when prefix test passes -> sessionStore.set(webContext, SESSION_POST_LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL_KEY, redirectOnFinish) (line 975) -> after successful token/profile validation in doFinishLogin, session value read back (lines 1329-1331) -> response.sendRedirect(HttpURLConnection.HTTP_MOVED_TEMP, redirectUrl) (line 1332) sends the victim's browser to the attacker-chosen origin immediately after authentication.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. Depends on the effective root URL lacking a trailing '/' (unverified for the configured-URL path; the request-derived path in getRootUrlFromRequest() is outside this snapshot). Whether a browser/library treats the resulting Location string as an off-site redirect in every variant was not executed. No Jelly/tests are present in the snapshot to confirm intended redirect semantics.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect'); insufficient URL validation

coverage_summary: Coverage: the assigned source scope contains 108 files / 17 Java files, all of which I read in full or with targeted line ranges: OicSecurityRealm (whole file), AnythingGoesTokenValidator, CustomOidcConfiguration, both crumb-exclusion classes, FailedCheckOfTokenException, OicAlgorithmValidatorFIPS140, OicCredentials, OicLogoutAction, OicServerConfiguration/Manual/WellKnown, OicUserDetails, ProxyAwareResourceRetriever, the ssl/* classes, pom.xml, Messages/config.properties and sampled help/docs. The P1 relation index (17 parsed files, 848 calls, 434 edges, syntactic name/arity candidates only, no control/data flow, semantic resolution, reachability, or SAST) was used solely for navigation and was verified against source text. No tests or Jelly views exist in this snapshot, so UI wiring and test-implied behavior were not reviewable. Jenkins core, pac4j 6.1.0 and Nimbus sources are outside the scope, so library-side enforcement (crumb handling, root-URL normalization, token signature verification) was reasoned about but not verified.
limitations: Static review only: no code executed, no tests/scanners run, no exploit payloads attempted; the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The snapshot lacks src/test and all .jelly views, so expected redirect validation behavior and UI wiring could not be cross-checked.

Jenkins core is not in scope, so I could not confirm whether Jenkins.getRootUrl()/JenkinsLocationConfiguration normalizes the URL to end with '/' or how getRootUrlFromRequest() formats the root URL — this determines whether the open-redirect precondition is commonly met.
The P1 relation index is syntax-only (no data flow/reachability); every indexed relation used was manually re-read in source, and unresolved calls (707) mean call-graph completeness is not claimed.
I could not consult upstream history, fixes, or CVE/CWE labels; resemblance to long-standing upstream patterns is based on source inspection, not history verification.

rejected_leads.lead: Inverted expiry test in OicServerWellKnownConfiguration.toProviderMetadata(): `wellKnownExpires.isBefore(now)` returns the cached metadata although the comment says 'configuration is still fresh' (lines 88-92), so the well-known document is re-downloaded every call while fresh and never refreshed once expired (contradicting docs 'regularly fetched').
rejected_leads.reason: Clear logic/consistency defect but no attacker-controlled input or privilege boundary: the well-known URL is administrator-configured and fetched server-side over TLS. Impact is stale provider metadata/extra requests (availability/configuration freshness), not a concrete security compromise; left as unconfirmed secondary lead.

rejected_leads.lead: EscapeHatchCrumbExclusion excludes /securityRealm/escapeHatch from CSRF unconditionally, unlike OicCrumbExclusion which first requires `sr instanceof OicSecurityRealm`.
rejected_leads.reason: The excluded path reveals no handler unless OicSecurityRealm is the active realm, in which case the crumb exclusion is intentional (comment explains the crumb is authentication-derived). No demonstrated cross-site impact; could not confirm whether the missing realm guard is a deviation from upstream.

rejected_leads.lead: handleTokenExpiration() parses `Authorization: Basic <b64>` with `.split(":")[1]` and direct Base64 decode before any validation (lines 1360-1372), and fetches `User.get2(...)` before the `user == null` guard.
rejected_leads.reason: Reaching this code requires a non-anonymous authentication (anonymous requests return at line 1354), so malformed headers only break the requester's own request (500). Robustness/DoS nuisance at most; no privilege or data-flow impact established.

rejected_leads.lead: Orphaned message key OicSecurityRealm.UsernameNotFound (Messages.properties line 22) suggests a possible removed null/empty-username check in doFinishLogin.
rejected_leads.reason: Message keys can be stale legacy strings; no removed-check can be proven from this snapshot, and a missing username leads to a failed user lookup rather than an authentication bypass. Not evidence enough for a candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: OicServerManualConfiguration.toProviderMetadata() advertises all HMAC and signature JWS algorithms for ID tokens (lines 157-166), raising an algorithm-confusion concern.
rejected_leads.reason: No source evidence in this snapshot that HMAC verification is attempted with asymmetric JWKS keys; pac4j/Nimbus behavior is out of scope and unverifiable here. Speculative.

summary: Reviewed the 108-file snapshot of the Jenkins oic-auth plugin (17 parsed Java files; all main Java sources read in full, key resource/docs files sampled). The strongest source-supported candidate is a post-authentication open redirect in OicSecurityRealm.getValidRedirectUrl(): the attacker-controlled `from` query parameter (or Referer) captured in doCommenceLogin is validated only by a string-prefix test against the Jenkins root URL and later used verbatim in response.sendRedirect in doFinishLogin. Because an absolute URL is resolved unchanged and only `startsWith(rootUrl)` is required, a URL such as `https://ci.example.com@evil.example/` (or `https://ci.example.com.evil.example/`) passes whenever the computed root URL has no trailing slash (notably when `rootURLFromRequest` is enabled, since a request-derived root URL is built without a trailing slash, or when the configured Jenkins URL lacks one). Other anomalies were examined and are either not attacker-controlled or too weak/unconfirmed to report. All findings are from static reading only; no runtime verification was performed.
